flagged.evidence: The step says that because the canonical quotient of Z_n(C) by B_n(C) is H_n(C), it is “not B_n(C).” The cited homology definition establishes that particular cokernel only; it does not exclude a different epimorphism Z_n(C) → B_n(C). Thus it does not refute the stated existential quotient claim. A valid witness is the complex Z → Q → 0 in Ab, with inclusion in degrees 1 to 0: Z_0=Q and B_0=Z, while every homomorphism Q → Z is zero, so B_0 is not a quotient of Z_0.

From f_n i_C e_C = i_D e_D f_{n+1}, the proof says: “Since e_C is epic, f_n i_C=i_D b_n for a unique morphism b_n.” Epicity of e_C gives uniqueness only after such a b_n exists; it does not itself supply the factorization through i_D. The cited factorization theorem states only that a morphism factors as an epic followed by a monic, not this lifting property. Existence can be recovered using that the image inclusion i_D is a kernel of a cokernel, but that argument is absent.

Step 1.1 defines d_n^P by saying “its ith projection is d_n^(i),” but the projection composite has source P_n, whereas d_n^(i) has source C_n^(i). The required equation is pi_i^(n-1) d_n^P = d_n^(i) pi_i^n. Dually, step 2.1 must use d_n^Q iota_i^n = iota_i^(n-1) d_n^(i), not say its composites with injections “are the differentials.” The cited product/coproduct definition requires precisely the typed equations p_i⟨f_i⟩=f_i and [f_i]iota_i=f_i, so it does not license the displayed construction as written.

The theorem is over an arbitrary abelian category, but the proof writes “On cycles it acts by z ↦ Z_n(f)(z)+Z_n(g)(z).” No element z of an arbitrary categorical object is defined. The cited additive-functor definition instead requires a homomorphism on hom-groups. The needed categorical proof that the induced map on the kernel and then its cokernel respects addition is omitted.

[L3] attributes “The kernel of f is the degreewise kernel complex” to prop-a-subcomplex-is-the-kernel-of-its-quotient-map. That proposition states only: “If S → C is a subcomplex, then the quotient map C → C/S has kernel S. Conversely, every monomorphism of complexes ... [is] a subcomplex.” It makes no assertion about kernels of arbitrary chain maps. The applicable scoped dependency is lem-the-kernel-of-a-chain-map-is-computed-degreewise, so [L3] and proof step 1.1 cite the wrong result.

The example assumes only a chain complex, hence an arbitrary abelian-category context, but concludes “every element of C_n is a cycle and every boundary is zero.” Objects of a general abelian category do not have elements in this sense. The result is true categorically, but the proof needs the kernel of the zero map to be C_n and the image of the zero map to be zero.
